§6ICF Components & Laser§f

§aBuild the laser assembly. Casework must be airtight or it won't assemble.§f

The ICF laser starts with a controller facing the reactor chamber. Behind it, place laser cells in a line, with flash bulbs adjacent to cells, capacitors adjacent to flash bulbs, and turbochargers adjacent to capacitors. Encase everything in ICF casing (like PWR casing), add ports for power, then right-click the controller to assemble.

§6Laser power§f: Calculated from capacitor and turbocharger count. Divide by 20 to convert HE/s to HE/t.

§6Stellar flux formula§f: Q = E x 10^-11, where Q is mB/t and E is reactor heat in TU. At max heat, 1 mB/t requires about 101.6 M TU/t.

§6Assembly check§f: If casing blocks show a gray border after right-clicking the controller, the laser assembled correctly. No border means something is wrong.

§ePS:§f Start with a conservative laser design and expand later. The ICF casing must be complete with zero gaps. Turbochargers are required for the laser to function.
